ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Equilateral triangle $ABC$ has side length $2$. A semicircle is drawn with diameter $BC$ such that it lies outside the triangle, and minor arc $BC$ is drawn so that it is part of a circle centered at $A$. The area of the “lune” that is inside the semicircle but outside sector $ABC$ can be expressed in the form $\sqrt{p}-\frac{q\pi}{r}$, where $p, q$, and $ r$ are positive integers such that $q$ and $r$ are relatively prime. Compute $p + q + r$.\n<image1>

A large semicircle with diameter BC is drawn below BC, outside the triangle. A smaller arc from B to C, centered at A, also lies below BC inside the semicircle. Reasoning: Since triangle ABC is equilateral with side length 2, BC = 2 and angle BAC = 60 degrees. The semicircle with diameter BC has radius 1, so its area is (1/2)π(1)^2 = π/2. The circle centered at A through B and C has radius 2, and sector ABC has central angle 60 degrees, so its sector area is (60/360)π(2)^2 = 2π/3. The equilateral triangle area is (sqrt(3)/4)(2)^2 = sqrt(3). Thus the circular segment of the A-centered sector lying inside the semicircle is sector area minus triangle area: 2π/3 - sqrt(3). The desired lune is the semicircle area minus this segment: π/2 - (2π/3 - sqrt(3)) = sqrt(3) - π/6. Therefore p = 3, q = 1, r = 6, so p + q + r = 10.
